security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when pointer masking is enabled via senvcfg.PMM (Ssnpm) for user mode, the page_fault_handler in trap.c reads tf_stval and uses it directly for VIRT_IS_VALID checks, signal delivery via call_trapsignal (SIGSEGV addr), and vm_fault_trap lookups — all without distinguishing whether stval holds the raw tagged address or the hardware-transformed (pointer-masked) address. The spec now clarifies that stval receives the pointer-masked address only for accesses subject to PM (data loads/stores), not for instruction fetches or implicit accesses. Code that blindly treats stval as always-raw or always-masked will misclassify faulting addresses under mixed PM/non-PM access scenarios.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: tf_stval used without smpm_unmask() or equivalent PM-awareness wrapper; VIRT_IS_VALID() applied to unmasked stval; call_trapsignal receiving hardware-masked stval as siginfo si_addr; page_fault_handler comparing stval >= VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS on masked address
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD's page_fault_handler and trap delivery code read stval (tf_stval) without pointer-masking awareness — if Ssnpm is ever enabled, the hardware writes a pointer-masked address to stval for data-access faults, but the kernel treats it as an untransformed address, risking incorrect VIRT_IS_VALID rejection of valid masked addresses or leaking tag bits to userspace via siginfo

findings.finding: tf_stval is read directly without any pointer-masking awareness. When Ssnpm is enabled (senvcfg.PMM != 0), hardware applies the ignore-transformation to stval for data load/store page faults but NOT for instruction fetch page faults (norm:pm_not_apply_implicit). The handler makes no distinction based on scause (data vs instruction fault), so it cannot determine whether the address in stval is raw or masked. Since FreeBSD currently does not implement Ssnpm, this is latent — but if PM were ever enabled (by future kernel code, M-mode firmware Smnpm, or bhyve VU-mode PM), the handler would silently treat masked and unmasked addresses identically.

VIRT_IS_VALID() is applied to stval without unmasking. For data page faults with PM enabled, stval holds the pointer-masked (transformed) address, not the raw tagged address. Since the ignore transformation sign-extends the PMLEN+1st bit, the masked address will typically be canonical — but the validity check is semantically operating on a transformed address while the caller (e.g., call_trapsignal) passes this same masked value as si_addr to userspace, creating confusion about which address type is being reported. Currently latent because FreeBSD does not enable PM.

Kernel-mode fault path compares stval >= VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS (0xffffffc000000000) without PM-awareness. If Smnpm (M-mode PM for S-mode) were ever enabled, a masked supervisor-mode data fault would have its upper bits zero-extended per the physical-address ignore transformation (norm:pm_ignore_pa), potentially misclassifying a user-space access as a kernel-space access or vice versa. Currently latent — FreeBSD does not configure menvcfg.PMM.

va = trunc_page(stval) is computed from the raw/unmasked stval for vm_fault_trap. When PM is enabled for data faults, the hardware-transformed address is the one that physically faulted, so using the masked stval is technically correct for the re-fault attempt. However, if the handler performed any address-range checks or comparisons between stval and the original user-supplied pointer (which it currently does not), inconsistencies would arise.

vm_fault_trap failure path calls call_trapsignal with stval as si_addr without PM-awareness. For a data page fault with PM enabled, si_addr receives the masked address; for an instruction page fault it receives the raw address. Userspace signal handlers (SIGSEGV handler receiving siginfo_t) cannot distinguish which type was delivered and may incorrectly attempt to unmask an already-unmasked instruction-fault address, or use a masked data-fault address as-is for debugging/memory analysis.

The entire page_fault_handler has no pointer-masking awareness. There is no smpm_unmask() wrapper, no PMLEN query, no scause-based discrimination between masked (data) and unmasked (instruction) stval values. The function uniformly assumes stval is always a raw, untransformed address. FreeBSD does not implement Ssnpm (no PMM configuration in senvcfg, no PM enable/disable paths, no boot-time PM setup), so this is currently a missing-feature gap rather than an active bug.
